questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Sam wants to ask the principal for a favour. Which message suits the principal best?
choices: Hey, gimme a ball at lunch, yeah?
Dear Mrs Nguyen, may I please borrow a ball at lunch?
Yo boss, can I grab a ball?
questions.explanation: A polite, full sentence with a greeting suits a principal. Slang suits friends.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Mia writes a letter to the mayor. Which word is the best fit for this formal audience?
questions.explanation: "Children" is a formal word. The others are casual words we use with friends.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which sentence states a fact (objective language)?
choices: Sydney is in New South Wales.
questions.explanation: You can check that Sydney is in New South Wales. The others are opinions.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Ben describes the beach. Which sentence shows his opinion, not a fact?
choices: The beach was crowded with 200 people.
questions.explanation: "Gorgeous" is what Ben feels. Long, sandy and a count of people can be checked.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: A recipe is built in stages. Which order is usual?
choices: Method first, then the ingredients list
Ingredients list first, then the method steps
A story first, then the ingredients
The method only, with no list
questions.explanation: A recipe lists what you need first. Then it gives the steps to follow.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Choose the best word to finish the sentence: ___ you finish your homework, you can play outside.
questions.explanation: "Once" shows time: homework first, then play.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which word best completes this sentence? We will cancel cricket ___ it rains.
questions.explanation: "If" shows a condition: cricket is cancelled only when it rains.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: On a website, you click a button and a list of pages appears. What is this called?
questions.explanation: A drop-down menu opens a list of choices when you click it.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which sentence is a complex sentence?
choices: We played cricket and Dad cheered.
Although it was raining, we played cricket.
We played cricket in the rain.
questions.explanation: "Although it was raining" cannot stand alone. It depends on the main clause "we played cricket".

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Mia smiled because she won the race. Which part is the clause that depends on the main clause?
questions.explanation: "Because she won the race" cannot stand alone as a sentence. "Mia smiled" is the main clause.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses direct speech?
choices: Tom told us about his hunger.
questions.explanation: Direct speech gives the exact words the person said inside quotation marks.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: "I like the zoo," said Priya. Which sentence reports this in indirect speech?
choices: Priya said I like the zoo.
Priya said she liked the zoo.
questions.explanation: Indirect speech has no quotation marks. "I like" changes to "she liked".

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: The wombat slept under the log. Which group of words is the prepositional phrase?
questions.explanation: "Under the log" begins with the preposition "under" and tells where the wombat slept.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: The kangaroo hopped very quickly across the paddock. Which words make the adverb group telling how it hopped?
questions.explanation: "Very quickly" is built around the adverb "quickly" and tells how it hopped.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which sentence is in the future tense?
choices: Our class is visiting the museum.
Our class will visit the museum.
questions.explanation: "Will visit" tells us it has not happened yet.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Choose the correct word. Yesterday the class ___ to the museum.
questions.explanation: "Went" is the past tense of "go". "Yesterday" tells us it already happened.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which word means almost the same as "enormous"?
questions.explanation: "Huge" and "enormous" both mean very big.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which word is the antonym (opposite) of "ancient"?
questions.explanation: "Ancient" means very old. "Modern" means new and up to date.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which sentence has the correct punctuation?
questions.explanation: A comma follows "said". The spoken words sit inside quotation marks, with the full stop inside them.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Leo asks a question. Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
choices: "Can we go to the beach." asked Leo.
"Can we go to the beach"? asked Leo.
"Can we go to the beach," asked Leo?
"Can we go to the beach?" asked Leo.
questions.explanation: The question mark goes inside the quotation marks. Then "asked" starts with a small letter.
